In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a HF diet may be beneficial to the cardiometabolic health of patients with type 1 or 2 diabetes and/or pre-diabetes.
the long-term effects are not yet clear and more research is needed to determine if HF diets are beneficial or detrimental to the management of pre-diabetes and type 2 diabetes.
the HF diet is superior to the LF diet in improving TAG levels and HDL-cholestrol levels, and in lowering diastolic blood pressures in patients with pre-diabetes and type 2 diabetes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HF diets are beneficial for the improvement of cardiometabolic risk in pre-diabetes and type 2 diabetes patients.
the long-term consumption of HF diets might be beneficial for subjects with pre-diabetes and diabetes, as it may reduce the risk for cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes.
HF diets may be more beneficial for pre-diabetic and type 2 diabetic individuals in terms of glycaemic and lipid control, but not in terms of body weight.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a HF diet is more effective than a LF diet in reducing the TAG and increasing the HDL-cho levels in patients with abnormal glucose metabolism.
a HF diet is a viable alternative to a LF diet in the management of pre-diabetic and type 2 diabetic subjects.
HF diets are associated with significant improvements in cardiometabolic risk markers, including TAG, HDL-cholestrol and diastolic pressure.
